name: Blessing Oil
description: A gentle all-purpose blessing oil of the kind kept by nearly every folk practitioner, used to bless people, homes, babies' cribs, new ventures and anything that needs a kindly hand laid upon it. Its soft blend of frankincense, rose and lavender draws on centuries of these plants being offered at shrines and churches. Think of it as a liquid benediction: warm, uplifting and safe for almost any occasion.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil
Rose absolute (or rose geranium) essential oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Drop the rose petals and lavender buds into the empty bottle as the 'bones' of the oil.
Add the essential oils one at a time, beginning with frankincense and sandalwood as the base, then lavender and rose.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Anoint the brow of anyone who asks for a blessing, trace a small equal-armed cross or pentacle on doorframes of a new home, dress white candles for blessing rites, and touch a drop to gifts, letters or cards before giving them.
chant: Blessed be the hand that gives, blessed be the one who lives; by rose and resin, light and grace, a blessing falls upon this place.
intention: I call blessing, kindness and good fortune upon all this oil touches.
timing: Sunday or Monday, in the waxing moon or at the full moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Absolutes are concentrated and can trigger allergies, so keep to the drops given; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Year-round; especially lovely at Imbolc (early Feb) and Midsummer (Jun) for blessing homes and families
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds.

name: Holy Anointing Oil
description: Inspired by the sacred anointing oil of Exodus 30, which blended myrrh, sweet cinnamon, calamus and cassia into olive oil to consecrate priests and holy vessels. Calamus is now avoided for safety, so this version uses olive oil, myrrh, frankincense and a tiny touch of cinnamon leaf. It is a solemn, resinous oil for consecration, ordination of your own practice and deep devotional work.
steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the frankincense and myrrh tears in the empty bottle.
Add myrrh first, then frankincense and cedar, and lastly the single drop of cinnamon leaf.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Hold the bottle up to candlelight or sunlight and pray or speak words of dedication from your own tradition.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Anoint the forehead, hands and feet before devotion or initiation, consecrate altars, chalices and prayer beads by tracing a sign upon them, and dress beeswax candles for sacred rites.
chant: Myrrh of mourning, incense of praise, holy oil of ancient days; set apart and sanctified, let the sacred here abide.
intention: I set this apart as holy and dedicate it to the Divine.
timing: Sunday at sunrise, or the full moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.3% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Cinnamon leaf oil is a strong skin sensitizer, so keep to the drops given and never substitute cinnamon bark or cassia oil, which are far harsher; olive oil turns rancid faster than jojoba, so make small batches and discard if it smells sharp. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Year-round; traditionally made at Easter/Ostara (Mar–Apr) or Yule (Dec) for the year's consecrations
interactions: Cinnamon leaf oil is rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains cinnamon oil, which is especially risky for cats.

name: Jinx Removing Oil
description: Jinx Removing is a classic hoodoo condition formula for breaking runs of bad luck, whether caused by someone's ill wishes or simple misfortune. Herbs like hyssop, rosemary and lemon have long been used in folk cleansing baths, and this oil brings them together in a sharp, clean blend. Use it when everything seems to go wrong at once.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Add the dried hyssop and a few grains of sea salt to the empty bottle.
Add lemon first, then rosemary, eucalyptus and peppermint.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress a white candle from the wick down to the base (drawing away) and burn it over seven nights, add a few drops to a cleansing bath with salt, anoint the soles of your shoes, and wipe a drop over the threshold sweeping outward.
chant: Jinx be gone and crossing break, every curse your leave now take; lemon, rosemary, hyssop pure, my luck returns, my path is sure.
intention: Every jinx, hex and run of bad luck upon me is broken and washed away.
timing: Waning moon, on Saturday or Tuesday.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 1.8% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Eucalyptus, peppermint and rosemary oils must never be used on or near the face of infants and young children, and people with epilepsy should avoid this blend; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Year-round; especially after the autumn equinox through Samhain (Sep–Oct) for clearing the year
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus, peppermint and eucalyptus oils, which are especially risky for cats.

name: Cast Off Evil Oil
description: A protective, exorcising oil in the spirit of old 'Cast Off Evil' and 'Devil's Shoestring' formulas, made entirely with gentle, skin-safe ingredients. Devil's Shoestring root was traditionally carried to 'trip up' evil before it could reach you, and here it rests in the bottle alongside protective basil and frankincense. It is used to drive off bad habits, unwanted influences and negative spirits.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the Devil's Shoestring and angelica root pieces in the empty bottle.
Add vetiver and frankincense first as the base, then juniper and basil.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress a black or white candle while speaking aloud the habit or influence you want to cast off, anoint your wrists and the back of your neck before difficult encounters, and rub a drop on a protective charm bag or under the doormat.
chant: Cast off evil, cast off harm, root and resin be my charm; what would bind me, trip and fall, I stand free above it all.
intention: I cast off every evil influence, habit and spirit that does not serve me.
timing: Waning or dark moon, Saturday in the hour of Saturn.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Use only linalool-type sweet basil oil, since estragole-rich basil is not safe at this amount; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Autumn into winter, Mabon to Yule (Sep–Dec), when the year naturally lets go
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds.

name: Fast Luck Oil
description: Fast Luck is one of the best-known hoodoo condition oils, prized by gamblers and shopkeepers for bringing luck quickly. Traditional recipes call for cinnamon, vanilla and wintergreen; this version drops wintergreen (which is toxic in quantity) and keeps cinnamon at a whisper, adding bright orange and bergamot. Use it when you need luck to arrive in a hurry.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the orange peel and allspice berry in the empty bottle.
Add vanilla first, then orange and bergamot, then the single drop of cinnamon.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress green or gold candles from base to wick (drawing toward you), anoint your palms before a game, sales call or interview, touch a drop to the cash register or wallet, and wipe it onto lottery tickets for a quick boost.
chant: Luck come fast and luck come quick, money stay and fortune stick; spinning wheel and rolling die, fortune turn and come to I.
intention: Good luck comes to me quickly and easily.
timing: Thursday or Sunday during the waxing moon, in the hour of Jupiter.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Cinnamon leaf oil is a strong skin sensitizer, so keep to the drops given and never substitute cinnamon bark or cassia oil, which are far harsher; use only bergamot labeled FCF (bergaptene-free), because ordinary bergamot can cause severe sunburn-like blistering; absolutes are concentrated and can trigger allergies, so keep to the drops given; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Year-round; especially spring and summer, Ostara to Lammas (Mar–Aug)
interactions: Cinnamon leaf oil is rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus and cinnamon oils, which are especially risky for cats.

name: Lucky Hand Oil
description: Named for the 'Lucky Hand' root (salep orchid), whose hand-like shape made it a famed gambler's charm in hoodoo. Because wild orchid roots are now endangered, this formula uses cinquefoil, the 'five-finger grass' that carries the same 'whatever five fingers can do' symbolism. It favors skill, deft hands and winning games of chance.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the cinquefoil and the lodestone or pyrite chip in the empty bottle.
Add patchouli first, then bergamot, basil and the single drop of nutmeg.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Rub a drop between your palms before playing cards, dice, bingo or any game of skill, anoint a gambling mojo bag, and dress a green candle with a five-fingered hand carved into it.
chant: Five fingers strong, five fingers sure, what my hand touches turns to more; the cards fall right, the dice run true, Lucky Hand, I work with you.
intention: My hands are skilled and lucky; I win fairly and well.
timing: Thursday or Sunday, waxing moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 1.7% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Use only bergamot labeled FCF (bergaptene-free), because ordinary bergamot can cause severe sunburn-like blistering; use only linalool-type sweet basil oil, since estragole-rich basil is not safe at this amount; nutmeg oil is potent, so keep to a single drop; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Year-round; summer, Midsummer to Lammas (Jun–Aug), for peak fortune
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus oil, which is especially risky for cats. It also contains nutmeg oil, to which cats are especially susceptible.

name: Double Fast Luck Oil
description: A stronger, doubled version of Fast Luck, traditionally used when ordinary luck work has not moved fast enough. The 'double' here comes from doubled allspice and a second warming note of ginger, which adds heat and speed without leaning on heavy skin sensitizers. It is a high-energy oil for urgent luck and sudden opportunities.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Drop two allspice berries (the 'double') and the pyrite chip into the empty bottle.
Add vanilla, then ginger, orange and lemongrass, finishing with the single drop of cinnamon.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress a green or gold double-action candle, anoint your shoes before heading out for an opportunity, add a drop to a lucky coin carried in your left pocket, and wipe onto business cards.
chant: Twice as fast and twice as bright, luck come running day and night; double up and double true, fortune finds me, through and through.
intention: Luck runs to me twice as fast and twice as strong.
timing: Sunday or Thursday, between the first quarter and full moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Cinnamon leaf oil is a strong skin sensitizer, so keep to the drops given and never substitute cinnamon bark or cassia oil, which are far harsher; lemongrass is a skin sensitizer, so use no more than about 4 drops per ounce; absolutes are concentrated and can trigger allergies, so keep to the drops given; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Spring through summer, Ostara to Midsummer (Mar–Jun)
interactions: Cinnamon leaf oil is rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus and cinnamon oils, which are especially risky for cats.

name: Prosperity Oil
description: Where Money Drawing pulls in cash, Prosperity Oil is about lasting abundance: a full table, a stable home and a growing store of wealth over time. Earthy patchouli, cedar and vetiver root the blend while bay laurel and orange invite growth, all herbs traditionally associated with Jupiter and the Sun. Use it for long-term financial health rather than quick wins.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the bay leaf piece and whole clove in the empty bottle.
Add vetiver and patchouli first, then cedar, bay laurel and orange.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress a green candle on a Thursday each week, anoint the corners of your bank book, wallet or business ledger, place a drop on seed packets before planting, and touch a drop to the four corners of your home's front door frame.
chant: Root and branch and golden fruit, abundance grow from deepest root; my cup is full, my table spread, my house is warm and richly fed.
intention: Abundance flows into my life steadily and stays.
timing: Thursday, waxing moon, in the hour of Jupiter.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Bay laurel oil can sensitize skin, so keep to the drops given; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Harvest season, Lammas to Mabon (Aug–Sep), and again at the turning of the calendar year
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus oil, which is especially risky for cats.

name: Success Oil
description: A bright solar oil for achievement, recognition and seeing your efforts pay off. Bay laurel crowned victors in ancient Greece and Rome, while frankincense and orange have long been tied to the Sun's power and honor. Use it when you have done the work and want the world to notice.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the bay leaf and calendula petals in the empty bottle.
Add frankincense first, then orange and bergamot, then bay laurel and ginger.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress an orange or gold candle before exams, auditions, launches or reviews, anoint your pulse points before important meetings, and touch a drop to your resume, portfolio or diploma.
chant: Laurel crown upon my head, golden sun and path ahead; all my labors bear their fruit, success is mine from crown to root.
intention: My work is recognized and I achieve my goals.
timing: Sunday in the hour of the Sun, waxing to full moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Use only bergamot labeled FCF (bergaptene-free), because ordinary bergamot can cause severe sunburn-like blistering; bay laurel oil can sensitize skin, so keep to the drops given; people allergic to ragweed or daisy-family plants may react to the calendula; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Summer, Midsummer to Lammas (Jun–Aug), when the Sun is strongest
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus oil, which is especially risky for cats.

name: Psychic Protection Oil
description: A shielding oil for empaths, readers and anyone who opens themselves to spirit work. Mugwort and lavender support psychic sight, while sandalwood, myrrh and rosemary form the protective 'wall' that keeps unwanted energies and entities out. Wear it before divination, mediumship or busy crowds.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil
Small black tourmaline or obsidian chip

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the mugwort and the tourmaline or obsidian chip in the empty bottle.
Add sandalwood and myrrh first, then lavender and rosemary.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Anoint the third eye, back of the neck and solar plexus before readings or mediumship, dress the edges of your tarot cloth, and touch a drop to your wrists before entering crowded or emotionally heavy places.
chant: Open eye but guarded gate, only light may enter straight; what is mine may come to me, all else turned back, so mote it be.
intention: My psychic senses are open and my energy is shielded and sovereign.
timing: Monday, full moon or any time before divination.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Rosemary oil must never be used on or near the face of infants and young children, and people with epilepsy should avoid this blend; mugwort should be avoided entirely in pregnancy and by people allergic to ragweed-family plants; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
bestTime: Autumn and winter, Samhain to Imbolc (Oct–Feb), when the veil is thin
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds.

name: New Moon Oil
description: A fresh, quiet oil for the first sliver of the lunar cycle, when intentions are seeded and plans begin. Jasmine and lemon balm (melissa) belong to the Moon's gentle side, while clary sage-like clarity comes from rosemary. Use it to anoint candles and journals as you set intentions for the month ahead.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil
Dried Jasmine flowers or a Moonstone chip

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the jasmine flowers or moonstone chip in the empty bottle.
Add sandalwood first, then lavender and rosemary, finishing with jasmine and melissa.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
If possible, set the bottle on a windowsill on the night of the new moon to receive the first darkness and returning light.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Anoint a white or silver candle while writing your intentions for the coming cycle, touch a drop to the pages of your journal or seed packets, and dab the heart before new-moon meditation.
chant: Silver seed in dark of night, grow with me toward the light; what I plant, the moon shall tend, from this beginning to its end.
intention: I plant the seeds of my intentions and trust them to grow.
timing: The new moon or within three days after; Monday.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes.
